findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is absent
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes the query returns at least one row. Site settings only have rows in the `site_settings` table once they've been changed from the default, so any site that never customized `embed_category` (the common case) will get an empty result set, and `[0]` will be `nil`, raising `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil` and aborting the migration. The same pattern is used for `uncategorized_category_id` on line 15. Both lookups need a nil-safe fallback.

findings.title: Host values interpolated directly into SQL in migration
findings.body: The migration builds `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` by interpolating `h`, which comes from the admin-editable `embeddable_hosts` site setting. A host entry containing a single quote (or any SQL metacharacters) will produce malformed SQL and abort the migration, and in general this is SQL injection into a migration. Use parameterized execution (e.g. `exec_insert` with binds) or at minimum `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally. If `host` is nil (e.g. the admin submits the create form with a blank host, so `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is nil in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of producing a validation error. Guard with `if self.host.present?`.

findings.title: update and destroy crash on unknown id instead of 404
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent id. `update` then calls `save_host(nil)` which raises NoMethodError on `host.host=`, and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`. Both should raise `Discourse::NotFound` / return 404 when the record is missing.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents creating two `EmbeddableHost` rows with the same host (the old site setting was a flat list where duplicates were harmless). Duplicates make `record_for_host` nondeterministic about which category an embedded topic lands in and clutter the admin UI. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive) and ideally a unique index in the migration.

findings.title: Case-sensitive host comparison against lower(host)
findings.body: `record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but never downcases the incoming `host`. A referer like `HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/page` yields `uri.host == "EVILTROUT.COM"`, which won't match the lowercase stored value, so embedding is wrongly rejected. Use `host.downcase` in the comparison.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The definitions happen to load globally so tests pass, but the files are named for the wrong fabricators, which will confuse anyone editing or looking up fabricators by filename and breaks the convention the test suite relies on. Swap the file contents back.

findings.title: Redundant/duplicated authorization filters
findings.body: Both new admin controllers declare `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, but `Admin::AdminController` already enforces admin access, and the routes are additionally wrapped in `AdminConstraint`. More notably `ensure_staff` would allow moderators (staff but not admins) while `AdminConstraint` allows admins — the layering is inconsistent; the controllers should rely on the standard admin controller behavior.
